notes:
The mixed marquee for the beat that is now THE REAL DENTASOURCE, and it carries the candid team frames too: the separate Our people strip was removed on 2026-09-06 and its eighteen tiles were folded in here, so one marquee shows the crew and the work instead of two showing them apart. THIS FILE CHOOSES WHICH ITEMS, NOT WHAT ORDER THEY RUN IN. The interleave moved into mixOrder() in panels.jsx on 2026-09-06, because the training beat's strip is merged in code from two manifests and no single file can decide the order for it; two rules for the same marquee is how they drift apart. The rule is: open on a video, space the videos evenly through the whole run. Everything between the clips is a photograph. EXTENDABLE: append either type, the component re-spaces it.
☠️ FIVE FRAMES ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT AND MUST NOT BE ADDED BACK AT TILE SIZE (ruled 2026-09-06). v033-8, v039-1, v039-2, v039-5 and v301-2 are 360 pixels wide at source with no larger copy anywhere. A tile on this strip renders up to 384 css px, which is 768 device px on a retina screen, so they would be served at less than half the resolution the tile needs and would sit visibly soft beside everything around them. They are documentary article photographs whose captions describe the exact frame, so they are never swapped for a lookalike and never upscaled. They keep their place IN the articles, where they render small; they only leave the large strips. The same five are listed in the machine readable `stripUnsafe` map on this file, keyed by filename, so a picker or a future builder can refuse them without parsing this paragraph. ☠️ NEITHER OF THESE TWO MANIFESTS IS GENERATED BY A SCRIPT: unlike crew-shots and training-media there is no builder to enforce the refusal, so the only guard is this key and whoever reads it.
☠️ tilePx IS THE DECISION NOW; THE stripUnsafe MAP BELOW IS DOCUMENTATION. tilePx is the largest CSS width a tile in this strip renders at, MEASURED on a production build at 1440 and at 390, not remembered: 384x288 css on a desktop (360x270 on a 390 phone). A file is too soft here when it cannot supply DPR 2 across that tile. The tiles are 4:3 with object-fit: cover and the source photographs are portrait, so the WIDTH is what binds: the image is scaled by max(tileW/w, tileH/h), which for a portrait source in a landscape box is tileW/w, and the test reduces to source width >= 2 x tilePx (768px here). Comparing against the source's LONG side instead gives the wrong answer on this strip.
